contentBlocks.title: 350,000 Grants to Be Reviewed in 2026 Crackdown
contentBlocks.description: Social Development Minister Dina Pule announced on 21 July 2026 that more than 350,000 social grants will be reviewed in the 2026/27 financial year as part of a major crackdown to save R1.5 billion in misspent funds.

contentBlocks.text: On 21 July 2026, Social Development Minister Dina Pule announced that more than 350,000 social grants will be reviewed in the 2026/27 financial year. The review is aimed at identifying grants that were incorrectly awarded, removing ineligible beneficiaries, and recovering approximately R1.5 billion in savings for the fiscus.

This is the largest grant review exercise since the SRD grant launched in 2020. According to SASSA, about 160,000 beneficiaries failed to complete their reviews last year, leading to automatic suspensions.

The review follows a Special Investigating Unit (SIU) report that found systemic weaknesses in SASSA's grant verification processes, particularly around identity verification, means testing, and bank verification for SRD grants.

items: R1.5 billion identified as potential savings from incorrect or fraudulent grants
350,000+ grants flagged across all grant types, not just SRD
160,000 beneficiaries already suspended for failing previous reviews
Biometric verification (eLife certification) now mandatory for all SRD applicants

contentBlocks.text: All grant types are affected, but the review is concentrated on:

items: SRD R370 Grant — highest volume of flagged applications
Child Support Grant — income threshold compliance
Older Person Grant — identity verification for age-75+ cohort

contentBlocks.title: Is your grant at risk?
contentBlocks.text: If you receive a letter from SASSA requesting a review, you must respond within 30 days. Failure to do so will result in automatic suspension without further notice.
How to Check If You Are Flagged

steps.title: Check your SMS and post
steps.description: SASSA sends a formal notification via SMS and post if you are flagged for review. Look for messages from 0800 60 10 11.

steps.title: Log into the SRD portal
steps.description: Visit srd.sassa.gov.za and enter your ID and phone number. A review flag will appear on your dashboard.

steps.title: Visit your nearest SASSA office
steps.description: If you cannot access the portal, visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID. Ask the officer to check your review status.

steps.title: Complete the review form
steps.description: Fill in the review form with your current financial and personal information. Supporting documents are required.

items: Certified copy of your South African ID
Latest 3 months bank statements showing all inflows
UIF deregistration letter (UI-19) if you were previously employed
NSFAS cancellation letter if you were previously a student

contentBlocks.title: Important: Deadline
contentBlocks.text: You have 30 days from receiving the review notification to submit all documents. Extensions are not granted. If you miss the deadline, your grant will be suspended and you will need to reapply.

items: Your grant continues — if SASSA confirms you are still eligible
Your grant is adjusted — if your income or circumstances have changed
Your grant is suspended — if you fail to respond or are found ineligible
Your case is referred for investigation — if fraud is suspected

faqs.question: I didn't receive a notification. Can I still be flagged?
faqs.answer: SASSA sends notifications via SMS and registered post. If your contact details changed, update them immediately on the SRD portal or at your local SASSA office.

faqs.question: What if my grant is suspended during the review?
faqs.answer: If your grant is suspended, you will receive written reasons. You can appeal the suspension within 90 days through the ITSAA appeal process. However, completing the review as requested is faster.

faqs.question: Will the SRD R370 be reviewed differently?
faqs.answer: SRD grants are reviewed monthly as part of normal processing. The 2026 crackdown is about identifying systemic fraud, not the monthly eligibility check. If you passed the monthly check, you are not necessarily flagged for review.

faqs.question: Can I lose my grant permanently?
faqs.answer: If SASSA determines you were never eligible, your grant will be cancelled and you may be asked to repay amounts received. If your circumstances changed, you may qualify for a lower grant amount.
